To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CheAs, a truncated form of the chemotaxis kinase CheA, is expressed by motile members of the family of enteric bacteria but not by nonmotile species, that CheAs is coexpressed with CheZ, the phosphatase that accelerates deactivation of the response regulator CheY, and that the coexpression of CheZ and CheAs may play a role in the chemosensory responses of enteric bacteria.
CheA, the histidine protein (HisPro) kinase of a two component signal transduction system, is expressed in two forms, CheAL and CheAs, by motile enteric bacteria.

CheAs, a short form of the chemotaxis protein CheA, is coexpressed with CheAL and CheY by motile enteric bacteria but not by closely related plant pathogens, suggesting a potential role of CheAs in the chemotaxis signaling pathway of motile enteric species.

the regulation of chemotaxis in the enteric species E. coli and Salmonella.
the coexpression of CheA, a histidine kinase that plays an essential role for bacterial chemotactic responses, by members of family Enterobacteraceae.
the regulation of the chemotaxis signaling pathway in the family Enterobactereaceae.
